lesson.title: Rushed Out Wide
lesson.hook: Pulled off the court and rushed, the big crosscourt and the angle feel like the way out. Only 6 in 10 of them land.
lesson.memHTML: Rushed? Deep and safe. In time? Make them run.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time you're pulled wide and late, hit deep and safe, through the middle or down the line. Save the angle for when you're there in time.

pro.label: The ATP's strategy coach on the middle
pro.moment: Studying Hawk-Eye heat maps of the pros, O'Shannessy finds the middle of the court is for building points and defending, not avoiding: balls through the middle tend to come back through the middle, which cuts the errors from chasing angles that aren't really there.
pro.read: When you're in trouble, the middle is a place to rebuild from, not a wasted ball.
pro.src: Brain Game Tennis, Craig O'Shannessy, Webinar 83: Playing the Middle of the Court

drill.name: Wide and late
drill.how: Your partner feeds wide to your forehand, then your backhand, some easy, some hard. Late: high and deep through the middle. In time: down the line.

steps.name: Pulled wide and late
steps.sit: Their crosscourt pulls you off the court on your forehand side, and you only just get there.
steps.payoff: Deep and safe lands every time, and all they can do is rally it back.
steps.principle: Rushed out wide, go deep and safe.
steps.why: Rushed, you can't swing fully, so the flat crosscourt and the angle land only 6 in 10, and the angle gives them your open court. High and deep through the middle lands every time and they can only rally it. Down the line works too (8 in 10), and so would a high, heavy crosscourt.
steps.take: Rushed out wide? Deep and safe.

lines.A: Only 6 in 10 land, and it opens your court. Passed.
lines.B: Also fine: 8 in 10, and they can only rally it.
lines.C: Right: lands every time. They can only rally it.
lines.D: Only 6 in 10 land when you're late.

steps.name: Wide, but in time
steps.sit: Pulled wide again, but this time you're there in time.
steps.payoff: In time, down the line stretches them, and you're set early for the next ball.
steps.principle: In time? Now make them run.
steps.why: Down the line goes away from them: they're stretched and you have 0.77 s on their next ball, with 8 in 10 landing. The middle is safe, but it's right to them. The angle and the flat crosscourt still land only 6 in 10.
steps.take: Wide but in time? Down the line.

lines.B: Only 6 in 10, and it opens your court.
lines.D: Right: they're stretched. You're set early.

steps.name: Late on the backhand
steps.sit: Their crosscourt backhand pulls you wide on your backhand side, and you're late.
steps.payoff: The deep slice through the middle gives you the most time to get back.
steps.principle: Late on the backhand: a deep slice through the middle.
steps.why: Late, the slice through the middle lands 8 in 10 and stays low and deep, so they can only rally it, and you have the most time to recover. The line leaves you only just in time. The angle lands 7 in 10 and opens your court.
steps.take: Late on the backhand? Deep slice, middle.

lines.A: Lands, but you're only just in time for the next.
lines.B: Lands 9 in 10, but less time to get back.
lines.D: Right: deep and low. The most time to recover.
